title: Judge Orders Release of Canadian Dentist Held in Minnesota
summary:
A Canadian dentist held by immigration officers in Minnesota is back home. A judge ordered him to be released right away.

Dr. William Lizardo, 32, was arrested on October 23 and held at Sherburne County Jail. He was ordered to leave the United States. On Sunday evening, he was finally released, his lawyer Hassan Ahmad said.

Judge Michael J. Davis wrote that the arrest broke Lizardo's constitutional rights. He noted Lizardo filed changes of address each time the couple moved.

In January, his request for permanent residency was denied because he had not provided a certified document from Ontario. Orders to appear at later hearings were sent to the wrong address, so Lizardo missed them and was arrested.

Lizardo asked to cancel the removal order because he had never received the hearing notices. A court granted that request on October 28. The judge said there was no reason to believe he was a flight risk and ordered his release. Lizardo now awaits a green card decision.
why_it_matters: Getting an address right matters, because a letter sent to the wrong place can change a family's life.

background_read: A green card lets a person from another country live and work in the United States for a long time.
To get one, people must send in papers and go to hearings, and officials must send hearing notices to the right address.
If notices go to the wrong address, a person can miss a hearing without knowing, and a judge can step in if detention is unfair.
